title: Sprint-lattice & contingency lanes for Q2 private tenant activations
creator: Samir Gupta
description: Objective: create a quarter-level sprint lattice and contingency lanes that sequence private/VPC/on-prem tenant activations while protecting SLOs and capacity budgets. Deliver a prioritized tranche plan, failure-budgeted rollout lanes, explicit contingency triggers (traffic ramp caps, rollback windows, canary health gates), and an ops-ready runbook for CS/SE/Eng. This ticket synthesizes stakeholder constraints (capacity commits, legal requirements for isolated tenants, and customer onboarding windows) into a runnable activation plan for Q2. Outcome: a tranche plan that maps cohorts to sprint buckets, an acceptance checklist for enabling a cohort, and an escalation playbook tied to observable signals.
acceptance_criteria: Tranche map created that assigns at least 3 customer cohorts to sprint buckets with reasons (capacity, contract priority, region)
Contingency lanes defined with explicit triggers: canary-failure-rate > 2%, 99th-latency breach of 1.5x target, or excess GPU utilization > 80% for 10m
Runbook published with steps for canary rollback, capacity burst request, and CS communication templates
Cross-team owners assigned for each lane (Eng/Infra/SE/CS) and dependent ENG tickets linked
Cost guardrails and failure budget per tranche documented and approved by finance
Smoke dashboards (dashboard links) identified and a pre-flight checklist included in the runbook
tasks: Workshop with Eng/Infra/SE to validate capacity hedging assumptions
Draft tranche prioritization criteria and run it past legal for regulated customers
Define canary metrics and create Grafana dashboards for preflight
Produce customer cohort activation templates (email, onboarding checklist, rollback notices)
Coordinate a dry-run activation with staging tenant and capture timings for rollback path

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive parallel activation reduces calendar time but increases blast radius and cost. We default to conservative parallelism (2 concurrent tranches) unless Eng signs off on autoscaler + KV-cache warmup optimizations. This ticket will feed the Q2 launch cadence and be the source of truth for CS enablement.
recent_decisions: Conservative parallelism: allow up to 2 concurrent tranche activations by default
Add legal signoff gate for regulated tenant cohorts before activation
Use canary window of 30 minutes for initial tranche validation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Autoscaler lag causes high latency during ramp. Mitigation: pre-warm capacity and enable temporary burst buckets; ENG-21105 to tune scaler.
Risk: Customer churn if activation issues affect critical paths. Mitigation: CS communication templates and rollback notice templates included in runbook.
Risk: Cost overshoot from inadvertent burst. Mitigation: finance-approved guardrails and automatic throttle at cost threshold.
